findings.title: Coverage's raw-count proof is not scoped to the product's shape, so other shapes' rows read as mismatches
findings.description: The two sides of the proof are scoped differently. `ledger_totals` filters by request shape (`r.dataset`, `r.symbols`, `r.stype_in`, `r.schema = ANY(tiers)`) plus `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`, but `raw_counts` counts **every** `tick_trade` row falling in the session windows — no instrument, unit, or shape predicate. `_session_row` (src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_coverage.py) builds `pairs` from the union of ledger and raw keys, so a row ingested under any other request shape yields `(instrument, 0, N)` → `Mismatch` → `EXIT_PARTIAL` from `tick_coverage` (src/manta_trading/cli/commands/tick_store_cmds.py), contradicting the module docstring's claim that a mismatch is "evidence of an out-of-band edit or a defect". This is reachable today: `adopt` accepts a job with arbitrary symbols (e.g., a continuous or raw-symbol ES job bought out-of-band) and `ingest` loads verified tier units regardless of shape, landing rows in `tick_trade` that the ES.FUT ledger never counts. It becomes routine the moment slice 231 adds GC to the universe (the universe and `FUTURES_PRODUCT_CALENDAR` comments anticipate this): CME metals sessions substantially overlap ES session windows, so every GC trade inside an ES session would be reported as an ES mismatch and `mt data tick coverage` would exit 3 on healthy data. Either scope the scan to instruments the shape's current units cover (e.g., join `tick_trade.unit_id` to current units of the shape), or state and mechanically guard the single-shape assumption the proof currently rests on.

findings.title: Populated-range edges: coverage widens the calendar query a day before `start` unnecessarily, and `_scope`'s upper bound can exceed the calendar span
findings.description: `build_coverage` calls `calendar_sessions` with `utc_midnight(start - timedelta(days=1))`. `TradingCalendar.sessions_between` requires **both** bounds inside the populated span (`_require_populated` in src/manta_trading/data/base/trading_calendar.py), and the extra day is unnecessary: `_fetch_sessions` selects sessions with `close >= start`, and a session dated `start` always closes on `start`, so it is included with a `midnight(start)` bound. The widening only adds a failure mode — `coverage --start <first populated session date>` exits 4 (`TickCalendarError` → storage) even though the requested range is populated. Symmetrically, `_scope` (src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_status_build.py) legitimately needs `midnight(held_day + 1)` to catch sessions opening at 22:00 on a held day, but that bound exceeds `last_close` when the newest held day is the calendar's last populated day, making `status` exit 4 instead of reporting. Both are edge cases (the calendar horizon normally extends ahead of ingested days); clamping the bounds to the populated span, or at least documenting the boundary behavior, would remove the surprise.

findings.title: `calendar_sessions` duplicates the calendar-failure scaffolding of `tick_calendar.product_session_days`
findings.description: The construct-`TradingCalendar` / `sessions_between` / map-`(OperationalError, CalendarNotFoundError, OutOfPopulatedRangeError)`-to-`TickCalendarError` / `finally: close()` scaffolding is reproduced almost line-for-line from `product_session_days` (src/manta_trading/data/tick/tick_calendar.py), including the identical message shapes and the `psycopg` import that exists only for the exception tuple. Only the inputs differ (calendar_id vs product, sessions vs touched days). A shared context manager (e.g., `with_calendar(url, calendar_id)` in `tick_calendar.py`) would keep the failure mapping in one place, since a future calendar-failure type must currently be added to both or the verbs will exit differently.

findings.title: `_session_row` rescans every ledger/raw key once per session — quadratic in range length
findings.description: `instruments = sorted({i for i, d in (*ledger, *raw) if d == day})` materializes and unpacks the full key tuples of both dictionaries for every session in the range. Work is O(sessions × total keys), and total ledger keys themselves grow with sessions, so a multi-year audit range (e.g., 1,250 sessions × ~50 instruments ≈ 60k keys) costs ~75M tuple unpackings — tens of seconds of pure-Python scanning plus per-session allocation churn. Grouping the dictionaries by day once (or iterating keys a single time into a per-day structure) makes it linear. Irrelevant at the days-to-months ranges coverage is typically run over, but the command takes an unbounded `--start/--end`.

findings.title: The `Settings`/`setup_logging` patch pair and its justification comment are copy-pasted across three test modules
findings.description: The same two-line patch (`manta_trading.cli.app.Settings`, `manta_trading.cli.app.setup_logging`) plus the same three-line comment about CliRunner's closed stream and logging handlers now exists in `_app_patches` here, the `no_key` fixture in test/integration/data/test_tick_ingest_cli.py, and the `settings` fixture in test/unit/cli/commands/test_data_tick_ingest.py. The comment itself says "as every CLI test does", which is the signal it should be a shared helper (a `contextmanager` in a cli-test support module or conftest fixture), so the workaround and its non-obvious rationale evolve in one place rather than drifting across copies.
